## Hinge question {#gac3-hinge .gac-lesson }

```{=html}
<div data-module="hinge" data-correct="3" class="hinge numeric-choices gac-hinge gac3-hinge">
<p class="hinge-question">The graph is <span data-math="y=f'(x)"></span>. What occurs on <span data-math="y=f(x)"></span> at <span data-math="x=1"></span>?</p>
<div class="hinge-toolbar"><div class="time" role="timer" aria-label="Time remaining">1:00</div><div class="toolbar"><label>Seconds <select class="timer-duration" aria-label="Question duration"><option>30</option><option>45</option><option selected>60</option><option>90</option><option>120</option></select></label><button class="timer-start primary">Start</button><button class="reset-question">Reset</button></div></div>
<div class="gac-hinge-layout"><svg data-gac3-hinge viewBox="0 0 430 320" role="img" aria-label="Graph of the first derivative: a downward-opening parabola touching the x-axis at x equals 1 and negative on both sides."></svg><div class="choices">
<button class="choice" data-answer="1" aria-pressed="false"><b>1</b><span>A local maximum.</span></button>
<button class="choice" data-answer="2" aria-pressed="false"><b>2</b><span>A local minimum.</span></button>
<button class="choice" data-answer="3" aria-pressed="false"><b>3</b><span>A horizontal point of inflection.</span></button>
<button class="choice" data-answer="4" aria-pressed="false"><b>4</b><span>No stationary point, because the function continues decreasing.</span></button>
</div></div>
<div class="hinge-bottom"><p>Fist on chest. Think quietly.<br>On “show”, hold up 1–4 fingers.</p><button class="reveal-answer primary">Reveal answer</button></div>
<div class="hinge-explanation" hidden><strong>3.</strong> <span data-math="f'(1)=0"></span>, with a negative derivative on both sides:<br>decreasing → horizontal → decreasing.</div>
</div>
```

::: notes
3 minutes, additional diagnostic. Correct answer 3. The graph shown is f', not f. Exact plotted derivative is f'(x)=−(x−1)^2, which corresponds to f(x)=−(x−1)^3/3+C. At x=1, f'=0 and f' is negative on both sides, giving a decreasing horizontal point of inflection. We cannot infer f(1)=0 from this graph. Equal units on the graph axes.

1 confuses the local maximum of the derivative graph with a maximum of f. 2 assumes derivative zero means minimum. 4 assumes that a stationary point must turn, ignoring the zero gradient at the point.

Use the default adjustable 60-second timer. Fist on chest; quiet independent thinking; simultaneous 1–4 fingers on the teacher's “show” cue. Expiry does not reveal. Reveal answer is separate; Reset clears choices and hides the answer.

Ready: ask for the derivative signs, then continue. Divided: compare paired reasons and revote before revealing. Needs explanation: draw negative, horizontal, negative tangent strokes and connect them to the plotted derivative before rechecking. The plotted polynomial derivative supports the inflection conclusion; no second-derivative calculation is needed in this lesson.

Craig Barton, diagnostic questions: https://tipsforteachers.co.uk/diagnostic-questions/ .
:::
